messages.author: 5ef0a4875982a9cc
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Using inla-r for training and test
parts:
Prediction is usually formulated as a missing data problem in Bayesian statistics. You can define one large model where the test data is included and the values you want predict are NAs. You will then get full posterior distributions for your predictions.

Patrik Waldmann

messages.author: 936ef8c6d12fc338
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: Using inla-r for training and test
parts:
Dear Clinton,

Sure, you can use one data set to fit the model and then predict it to another dataset. However. INLA does the model fitting and prediction in one go. So you need to combine the training data and the test data into one data set. And set the response variable of the test part to NA. Then the test data is not used to fit the model.

Best regards,

I'm an INLA beginner, but when I asked a related question, I found out that you can also train using the training set and then sample from the predictive posterior distribution to evaluate the model with respect to the test data.

If the inla result was computed with control.compute=list(config=TRUE) you can use inla.posterior.sample to get samples.
